Of this child and his birth order relative to Alvin Smith, Joseph Smith Sr. said in 1833: “The Lord, in his just providence has taken from me, at an untimely birth, a son & this has been a matter of affliction; but the Lord’s ways are just. My next son, Alvin . . . was taken from us in the vigour of life, in the bloom of youth” (Joseph Smith Sr., Patriarchal Blessing Book 1, page 1, Patriarchal Blessings, 1833–2011, Church History Library, Salt Lake City).

After Alvin’s death in 1823, neighbors alleged that the Smiths had disinterred Alvin’s body to sell it for anatomical study. Neighbors later spread rumors that the Smiths wanted to bring the body to the site where the plates were buried to satisfy the angel’s demands. Rumors of the disinterment upset the family so much that even in his poverty, Joseph Sr. purchased advertisements in the local newspaper, hoping to silence the allegations (Dean C. Jessee, “Joseph Knight’s Recollection of Early Mormon History,”BYU Studies,vol. 17, no. 1 [Autumn 1976], 31; Joseph Smith Sr.,“To the Public,”Wayne Sentinel,vol. 2, nos. 1–6 [September 29–November 3, 1824]).
